data.cultural_impact: The name Dawid in Islamic culture is rooted in the rich history of the prophets and eminent figures of the past. Dawid, meaning "beloved by God," is the Arabic form of the Hebrew name David from the Old Testament in the Bible. In Islamic tradition, he is recognized as a prophet and a renowned figure for his wisdom, courage, and unwavering faith in Allah.

It emphasizes the importance of being in a constant state of surrender to Allah's love, guidance, and protection.

historical_references.reference: Ibrahim ibn al-Abbas narrated that when Dawud (David) was made the king of Judah, he was a young man who tended sheep for Saul. Dawud was a man of great courage and strength, and when Goliath, the Philistine giant, challenged the Israelites to send out a man to fight him, Dawud accepted the challenge. He killed Goliath with a stone and a sling, and was rewarded by Saul with the hand of his eldest daughter, Michal.
historical_references.context: The story of Dawud (David) is found in the Hebrew Bible, specifically in the Books of Samuel.

historical_references.reference: The name Dawud is also mentioned in the Quran, where it is written that Allah granted him the kingdom and granted him Solomon as a successor and helper. Dawud is also known as a noble prophet and a companion of Sulayman (Solomon) in the construction of the Temple in Jerusalem.
historical_references.context: The Islamic interpretation of the story of Dawud can be found in the Quran, specifically in Surah Al-Anbiya (21:78-81).
